segments.text: Of all the miracles Muslims believe in... this is the one people find hardest to say out loud. The moon... the actual moon... split in two. And the men who saw it never stopped telling it.
segments._shot: full moon huge over a dark desert horizon

segments.text: This is the night... the moon was split.
segments.title: THE MOON
segments._shot: slow drifting clouds crossing a bright moon

segments.text: Makkah, before the migration. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, had been preaching for years, and the leaders of his city wanted proof. So they demanded a sign... something no man could fake. Not words. The sky.
segments._shot: rugged dark mountains under deep night

segments.text: The people of Makkah asked him to show them a sign... and he showed them the splitting of the moon. That demand, and what followed it, sits in Sahih al-Bukhari... the most rigorously authenticated book in Islam after the Qur'an.
segments._shot: star-filled sky, one bright object rising

segments.text: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, was standing there. We were with the Prophet at Mina, he said... a valley just outside Makkah. And the moon was split. One piece went toward the mountain. And the Prophet said... bear witness. Be witnesses to this.
segments._shot: moonlight over a jagged mountain ridge

segments.text: And the Qur'an itself carries the event, in a chapter named The Moon. The Hour has come near... and the moon has split.
segments._shot: the moon reflected, trembling, on dark water

segments.text: Notice the order of that verse. Not... look what happened. But... the Hour has come near. The split moon was never just a spectacle. It was a clock, striking once... reminding every eye that looked up that this world has an end.
segments._shot: slow clouds swallowing the moon into darkness

segments.text: The same moon hangs over you tonight... whole, quiet, patient. The men who saw it torn in two changed their lives. It has never needed to happen twice.
segments._shot: calm night landscape, moonlit, vast and still
